The image is a science figure. Its parts are: "Hokkaido region" (printed label "Hokkaidō"); "Tohoku region" (printed label "Tōhoku"); "Kanto region" (printed label "Kantō"); "Chubu region" (printed label "Chūbu"); "Kansai region" (printed label "Kansai"); "Chugoku region" (printed label "Chūgoku"); "Shikoku region" (printed label "Shikoku"); "Kyushu region" (printed label "Kyūshū"); "Okinawa inset region" (printed label "(Okinawa)"). For each part, using the part name exactly as given, return:
- kind: "area" for a part with a filled interior; "thin" for a part drawn as a line or a strip too narrow to hold a fingertip; "group" for a part made of other listed parts.
- members: for a group, the listed parts it is made of; otherwise empty.
- parent: the listed part this part sits inside, or empty.
- instances: every place the part appears, in the main drawing and in any inset or enlarged view. A group has no instances. For each instance, 1 to 3 points spread across its filled interior, each as far as possible from the part's edges. For an elongated part such as a vessel or a stalk, put the points on its midline along its length. Never put a point on label text, a leader line or an outline, or on the part's tip or edge.
Coordinates are on a 0 to 1000 grid of this image: x from the left edge, y from the top edge.
